Full-time | $65,000 to $85,000 | Remote

Do you like solving accounting puzzles?

Some accountants like maintaining clean books.

You like figuring out why they aren't clean in the first place.

Breakwater Accounting & Advisory is looking for a Cleanup Manager who gets genuine satisfaction from taking messy financials, figuring out what happened, and turning them into books that leadership can actually trust.

You investigate. You trace the money. You ask questions. You test theories. You rebuild accounts. You find the root cause. Then you create a clean, reliable financial picture that the client and our ongoing accounting team can trust.

And then?

You move on to the next puzzle.

This is a role for someone who enjoys variety and problem solving. You'll work on multiple cleanup projects at once, diving into each one, solving the problem, creating a clean handoff, and moving forward.

What You'll Do

Find the mess. Figure out what happened. Fix it. Prove it's right. Move on to the next puzzle.

Investigate and solve

  • Dig into messy financial records to understand what happened and why.
  • Trace transactions to uncover errors, missing information, and broken processes.
  • Develop practical cleanup plans and work through them to completion.
  • Reconstruct financial activity when the existing records don't tell the full story.

Prove the numbers are right

  • Reconcile and substantiate major balance sheet accounts including cash, payroll, loans, revenue, prepaids, accruals, fixed assets, and equity.
  • Create supporting schedules and documentation that show why the numbers are right.
  • Go beyond “it balances” to create financials that are accurate, explainable, and defensible.

Make the books make sense

  • Redesign charts of accounts when they no longer serve the business.
  • Organize financial reporting so business owners can understand what is actually happening.
  • Identify the story behind the numbers and make that story easier to see.

Fix what caused the problem

  • You'll reverse-engineer workflows such as invoicing, payroll, inventory, and expenses to understand where things went wrong.
  • Help create better processes so the same problem doesn't show up again.

We don't believe in cleaning up the same mess twice.

Use your accounting and technology expertise

  • QuickBooks Online is one of your primary tools. You'll troubleshoot complex issues, untangle stubborn balances, and find solutions when the obvious answer isn't working.
  • We're a tech-forward team. We use modern accounting technology and AI to solve problems and improve efficiency. You don't need to be an AI expert. You do need to be curious and willing to try new approaches.

Communicate and collaborate

  • Work directly with clients to ask smart questions, gather missing information, explain complicated accounting issues, and keep projects moving.
  • Collaborate with the Breakwater team, document your work, and create clean handoffs to the ongoing accounting team.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting.
  • 5+ years of high-level accounting, audit, or full-cycle bookkeeping experience.
  • Strong understanding of how balance sheets actually work.
  • Experience with accruals, revenue recognition, depreciation, amortization, and other complex accounting concepts.
  • Prior reviewer, senior accountant, audit, or similar experience.
  • Proven experience cleaning up messy or inaccurate financials.
  • Expert-level QuickBooks Online proficiency.
  • Excellent investigative and problem-solving instincts.
  • Ability to stay focused and see a problem through to completion.
  • Confidence communicating complex financial issues to non-accountants.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects without losing the details.

Experience in an outsourced, multi-client accounting environment is a plus, as is experience with tools such as Xero, Dext, Ramp, BILL, Gusto, ACS/Realm, and advanced Excel.

Why Breakwater?

At Breakwater, you'll work with businesses and nonprofits across a variety of industries, so no two cleanup projects are exactly alike.

You'll join a team that values being proactive, positive, prepared, purposeful, protective, and principled.

You'll also get:

  • $65,000 to $85,000 salary
  • Full-time employment
  • Five weeks of PTO
  • Benefits
  • A collaborative, supportive team
  • Challenging accounting work where you get to solve problems every day

If you read this and thought, “that sounds like fun!” we want to meet you.

Accounting Management:

- Ensure compliance with accounting principles, standards, and regulations.
- Prepare and review financial statements, reports, and records.
- Conduct regular audits and resolve discrepancies.
- Perform detailed reconciliation checks to ensure accuracy and completeness of financial data.

Migration Projects:

- Plan and execute data migration projects from various accounting software (QuickBooks, Sage, Xero) to Zoho Books.
- Develop customized migration strategies tailored to each client's business operations.
- Ensure zero downtime and seamless business operations during live migration processes.

Project Management:

- Monitor project progress and report on key metrics.
- Maintain detailed documentation of migration processes and procedures.

Continuous Improvement:

- Recommend and implement improvements to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of migration projects.

Nice to Have

  • Strong hands-on experience with Zoho Books

  • Experience in SaaS, fin-tech, accounting firm

  • Experience with data migration projects

  • Advanced Excel skills including: Power Query, Power Pivot

  • Experience in building SQL reports

Work Setup

  • Remote (BYOD): Must have a personal laptop/PC and a stable internet connection

  • Working Hours: EST time zone (5 AM – 2 PM EST)

  • Work Environment: High-autonomy, ownership-heavy, and fast-paced


Benefits

Salary Range

  • Fully remote work with location flexibility

  • Medical insurance benefits (post-confirmation)

  • 24 days of paid time off (PTO)

  • Opportunity to work with a Canadian employer, compliant with international standards

  • Strong focus on professional growth and continuous learning

    What would it take for a financial controller to hand you a company's payables and reconciliations and never need to check behind you?

    On a typical day you might clear the team's reimbursement queue and prepare a supplier payment run in Xero in the morning, work a Stripe settlement mismatch down to its source after lunch, and send the Financial Controller a balance sheet workpaper with a flagged query and your recommended fix before the end of day.

    About Contour

    We started in 2020 with a handful of students and a belief that great education should not be out of reach. Today we operate across three brands with 8,000+ students and 425+ team members: roughly 100 in India and 325 onshore in Australia. The India team runs publishing, student experience, CRM and technology, operations, and people and culture, and this role sits with the group finance function.

    Every company at this scale runs on someone who keeps the money side exact. This is that seat.

    About This Role

    You are the accountant who runs Contour's transactional finance day to day: accounts payable, team member expense reimbursements, and account reconciliations, with balance sheet management as the part that stretches you. The balance sheet work is also why this role needs a qualified accountant rather than a bookkeeper. You report to the Financial Controller, who owns statutory reporting, tax, and sign-off on the monthly close. Everything underneath is yours: what gets paid, what gets reimbursed, and whether every account reconciles.

    Two habits separate a strong hire here from a competent one. First, judgement about when to ask and when to act: you raise a blocker early instead of sitting on it, you do not guess on anything material, and once you have the answer you execute without follow-up. Second, you treat an unreconciled difference as a problem to run to ground, not a number to plug.

    You start solo in group finance. The work grows with your tenure: management accounting first, then analytical and reporting work, and over time designing the processes rather than running them.

    The role matters now because the volume is real: supplier invoices, team member expense claims, and student payments settling through Stripe every day, all of which has to be accurate and on time. By the end of month three, you will have accounts payable and reimbursements running on a predictable cycle with no backlog, bank and Stripe reconciliations current, balance sheet accounts reconciled monthly with workpapers ready for review, and the recurring work documented well enough that someone else could run it from your notes. What you build in those first months becomes how Contour runs this function as it scales.

    Where the work lives

    • Xero:the ledger lives here, so clean coding, up-to-date bank feeds, and tidy reconciliations are the baseline.

    • Stripe:student payments settle here, so settlements and fees get reconciled back to Xero, line by line.

    • HubSpot and monday.com:the rest of the business runs here, so billing queries and task status move through them, and updating your status there is how a remote team stays coordinated.

    What You Will Do

    • Run accounts payable end to end.Verify supplier invoices, code them correctly in Xero, prepare payment runs, and keep suppliers paid on time.

    • Process team member expense reimbursements.Check claims against policy, query anything that does not look right, and keep turnaround predictable so people are not left waiting on their own money.

    • Own account reconciliations.Bank accounts, Stripe settlements, and key ledger accounts, kept current every month.

    • Manage balance sheet accounts.Maintain the reconciliations and workpapers that support the monthly close, and flag anything material to the Financial Controller before close week.

    • Be the day-to-day contact for auditors.Pull samples, walk them through the workpapers, and keep internal controls tight enough to hold up under inspection.

    • Document what you run.Turn the recurring work into written steps so the function stays reliable as it grows.

    If a better way exists to do something we are doing manually, make the case and we will back it.


    Requirements

    What You Need

    • A commerce degree plus CA Inter, CMA Inter, or part-qualified ACCA (discontinued is fine), or an M.Com, and 2 to 4 years of hands-on accounting work

    • Reconciliation experience across bank, supplier, or settlement accounts

    • Working proficiency in Xero: coding transactions, running bank feeds and reconciliations, and pulling reports without help

    • Balance sheet exposure: you have maintained balance sheet reconciliations or prepared workpapers for a month-end close

    • Sharp written English and comfort working across the India and Australia time difference. Much of your work with the Financial Controller is asynchronous, so a written query or a workpaper note has to land as intended the first time

    Nice to Have

    • Australian accounting exposure: GST, BAS, or work for Australian clients

    • Experience supporting a statutory audit

    • Reconciliation work with Stripe or another payment platform

    • Experience in a startup or multi-brand environment

    The Kind of People Who Thrive Here
    The people who do well here see a gap and close it without being asked, holding the bar even when the clock is short. They give a direct read on the work in front of them, including when it's wrong, and when their own idea doesn't hold up, they say so and bring a better one. They build something that keeps running after they step back. Problems here don't show up on schedule or in the same shape twice, and they'd rather make the right call on limited information than let something break while they wait for a sign-off. That's the job. They name the blocker and the ask the moment they have it, on a call or a text, because decisions get made on the information you bring.

    Contour's current cluster heads started as team leads. The path from operator to leader is real here.

    What good looks like

    • Nothing needs chasing:suppliers and team members get paid without following up.
    • The close is boring:month-end arrives with nothing left to find.
    • Trusted at a distance:the Financial Controller knows where things stand without having to ask.

    Benefits

    Fully remote, anywhere in India. Compensation is competitive and benchmarked to the role and your experience, and we discuss it openly early in the process. From application to offer: a short screen, a technical assessment, a culture conversation with our People team, and a final interview with the Financial Controller, in about four weeks.
